title: Understanding Principal Components
text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It does this by transforming the data into a set of orthogonal (uncorrelated) variables called principal components.

title: Singular Values and Principal Components
text: The singular values in PCA represent the amount of variance captured by each principal component. The larger the singular value, the more variance that component captures.

title: Identifying the First Principal Component
text: The first principal component is the one with the largest singular value. It captures the most variance in the data.

title: Determine the First Principal Component
text: Given that PC \alpha has a singular value of $$48.42$$ and PC β has a singular value of $$36.31$$, which principal component captures more variance?

title: Evaluating the Statement
text: Since PC \alpha has a larger singular value than PC β, it captures more variance and is the first principal component. Therefore, the statement that PC \alpha is the first principal component is true.
